review.title: Administrative agencies and unconstitutional statutes
review.plain: An administrative agency has no power to declare a statute unconstitutional, or to declare a statute unenforceable or refuse to enforce it as unconstitutional or barred by federal law, unless an appellate court has so determined.
limits: has no power

provisions.what: An administrative agency has no power to declare a statute unenforceable, or refuse to enforce a statute, on the basis of it being unconstitutional
provisions.binds: An administrative agency, including an administrative agency created by the Constitution or an initiative statute
forbids: declare a statute unenforceable, or refuse to enforce a statute, on the basis of it being unconstitutional
exceptions: unless an appellate court has made a determination that such statute is unconstitutional

provisions.what: An administrative agency has no power to declare a statute unconstitutional
provisions.binds: An administrative agency, including an administrative agency created by the Constitution or an initiative statute

provisions.what: An administrative agency has no power to declare a statute unenforceable, or to refuse to enforce a statute on the basis that federal law or federal regulations prohibit the enforcement of such statute
provisions.binds: An administrative agency, including an administrative agency created by the Constitution or an initiative statute
forbids: declare a statute unenforceable, or to refuse to enforce a statute on the basis that federal law or federal regulations prohibit the enforcement of such statute
exceptions: unless an appellate court has made a determination that the enforcement of such statute is prohibited by federal law or federal regulations

review.title: Salaries of elected state officers and judges
review.plain: Salaries of elected state officers may not be reduced during their term. Judges' base salaries are fixed from January 1, 1981; the Legislature may raise them or end prospective increases but shall not reduce a judge's salary during a term below the highest level paid.
powers: The Legislature may prescribe increases in those salaries during a term of office
may terminate prospective increases in those salaries at any time during a term of office
limits: salaries of elected state officers may not be reduced during their term of office
shall not reduce the salary of a judge during a term of office below the highest level paid during that term of office

provisions.what: Salaries of elected state officers may not be reduced during their term of office
forbids: reducing salaries of elected state officers during their term of office
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivision (b)

provisions.what: Laws that set these salaries are appropriations
Beginning on January 1, 1981, the base salary of a judge of a court of record shall equal the annual salary payable as of July 1, 1980, for that office had the judge been elected in 1978
The Legislature may prescribe increases in those salaries during a term of office, and it may terminate prospective increases in those salaries at any time during a term of office
The Legislature shall not reduce the salary of a judge during a term of office below the highest level paid during that term of office
forbids: reduce the salary of a judge during a term of office below the highest level paid during that term of office

provisions.what: Laws setting the salaries of judges shall not constitute an obligation of contract pursuant to Section 9 of Article I or any other provision of law

review.title: Suits against the State
review.plain: Suits may be brought against the State in the manner and in the courts directed by law.

provisions.what: Suits may be brought against the State in such manner and in such courts as shall be directed by law
conditions: in such manner and in such courts as shall be directed by law

review.title: English as the official language
review.plain: English is the official language of California. The Legislature shall enforce this section and make no law that diminishes or ignores the role of English. Residents and those doing business in California may sue the State to enforce it.
rights: shall have standing to sue the State of California to enforce this section
powers: shall have jurisdiction to hear cases brought to enforce this section
The Legislature may provide reasonable and appropriate limitations on the time and manner of suits brought under this section
limits: shall make no law which diminishes or ignores the role of English as the common language of the State of California

provisions.what: English is the common language of the people of the United States of America and the State of California. This section is intended to preserve, protect and strengthen the English language, and not to supersede any of the rights guaranteed to the people by this Constitution
English is the official language of the State of California
The Legislature shall enforce this section by appropriate legislation
requires: enforce this section by appropriate legislation

provisions.what: The Legislature and officials of the State of California shall take all steps necessary to insure that the role of English as the common language of the State of California is preserved and enhanced
provisions.binds: The Legislature and officials of the State of California
requires: take all steps necessary to insure that the role of English as the common language of the State of California is preserved and enhanced

provisions.what: The Legislature shall make no law which diminishes or ignores the role of English as the common language of the State of California
forbids: make any law which diminishes or ignores the role of English as the common language of the State of California

provisions.what: Any person who is a resident of or doing business in the State of California shall have standing to sue the State of California to enforce this section
provisions.holder: Any person who is a resident of or doing business in the State of California

provisions.what: The Courts of record of the State of California shall have jurisdiction to hear cases brought to enforce this section
provisions.holder: The Courts of record of the State of California

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide reasonable and appropriate limitations on the time and manner of suits brought under this section

review.title: Retirement allowances of certain elective officers
review.plain: Legislators' Retirement System allowances of certain elective state officers (not judges or legislators), and of their survivors or beneficiaries, shall not be increased or affected by compensation changes on or after November 5, 1986. It states the people's intent and findings against windfall benefits.
limits: shall not be increased or affected in any manner by changes on or after November 5, 1986, in the compensation payable

provisions.what: The retirement allowance for any person whose credited service in the Legislators’ Retirement System was rendered as an elective officer of the State whose office is provided for by the California Constitution, other than a judge and other than a Member of the Senate or Assembly, and whose retirement allowance is calculated on the basis of the compensation payable to the officer holding the office which the member last held prior to retirement, or for the survivor or beneficiary of such a person, shall not be increased or affected in any manner by changes on or after November 5, 1986, in the compensation payable to the officer holding the office
forbids: increasing or affecting the retirement allowance in any manner by changes on or after November 5, 1986, in the compensation payable to the officer holding the office which the member last held prior to retirement

provisions.what: This section shall apply to any person, survivor, or beneficiary described in subdivision (a) who receives, or is receiving, from the Legislators’ Retirement System a retirement allowance on or after November 5, 1986, all or any part of which allowance is calculated on the basis of the compensation payable to the officer holding the office which the member last held prior to retirement

It is the intent of the people to restrict retirement allowances to amounts reasonably to be expected and to preserve the basic character of earned retirement benefits while prohibiting windfalls and unforeseen advantages; this section shall not be construed as a repudiation of a debt nor the impairment of a contract for a substantial and reasonable retirement allowance

The people and the Legislature find and declare that the dramatic increase in the retirement allowances of persons described in subdivision (a) which would otherwise result when the compensation for those offices increases on November 5, 1986, or January 5, 1987, are not benefits which could have reasonably been expected

review.title: California Citizens Compensation Commission
review.plain: Creates a seven-member commission appointed by the Governor that establishes and adjusts the annual salary and medical, dental, insurance and similar benefits of state officers by majority resolution, sets who may serve, requires open meetings, and lists factors it shall consider.
limits: No current or former officer or employee of this State is eligible for appointment to the commission
a resolution shall not be adopted or take effect in any year that increases the annual salary of any state officer

provisions.what: The California Citizens Compensation Commission is hereby created and shall consist of seven members appointed by the Governor
The commission shall establish the annual salary and the medical, dental, insurance, and other similar benefits of state officers
requires: establish the annual salary and the medical, dental, insurance, and other similar benefits of state officers

provisions.what: Three public members, one of whom has expertise in the area of compensation, one of whom is a member of a nonprofit public interest organization, and one of whom is representative of the general population

No person appointed pursuant to this paragraph may, during the 12 months prior to his or her appointment, have held public office, either elective or appointive, have been a candidate for elective public office, or have been a lobbyist, as defined by the Political Reform Act of 1974
provisions.binds: No person appointed pursuant to this paragraph

provisions.what: Two members who have experience in the business community, one an executive of a corporation incorporated in this State which ranks among the largest private sector employers in the State and one an owner of a small business in this State
Two members, each of whom is an officer or member of a labor organization
The Governor shall strive insofar as practicable to provide a balanced representation of the geographic, gender, racial, and ethnic diversity of the State in appointing commission members

The Governor shall appoint commission members and designate a chairperson for the commission not later than 30 days after the effective date of this section; within 15 days of any vacancy, the Governor shall appoint a person to serve the unexpired portion of the term

The terms of two of the initial appointees shall expire on December 31, 1992, two on December 31, 1994, and three on December 31, 1996, as determined by the Governor. Thereafter, the term of each member shall be six years
No current or former officer or employee of this State is eligible for appointment to the commission
forbids: appointment of a current or former officer or employee of this State to the commission

provisions.what: Public notice shall be given of all meetings of the commission, and the meetings shall be open to the public
requires: Public notice shall be given of all meetings of the commission
the meetings shall be open to the public

provisions.what: On or before December 3, 1990, the commission shall, by a single resolution adopted by a majority of the membership of the commission, establish the annual salary and the medical, dental, insurance, and other similar benefits of state officers

At or before the end of each fiscal year, the commission shall, by a resolution adopted by a majority of the membership of the commission, adjust the medical, dental, insurance, and other similar benefits of state officers, effective on and after the first Monday of the next December

At or before the end of each fiscal year, the commission shall adjust the annual salary of state officers by a resolution adopted by a majority of the membership of the commission, effective on and after the first Monday of the next December

A resolution shall not be adopted or take effect in any year that increases the annual salary of any state officer if the Director of Finance certifies a negative balance in the Special Fund for Economic Uncertainties
conditions: if, on or before the immediately preceding June 1, the Director of Finance certifies to the commission, based on estimates for the current fiscal year, that there will be a negative balance on June 30 of the current fiscal year in the Special Fund for Economic Uncertainties in an amount equal to, or greater than, 1 percent of estimated General Fund revenues

provisions.what: In establishing or adjusting the annual salary and benefits, the commission shall consider all of the following
requires: The amount of time directly or indirectly related to the performance of the duties, functions, and services of a state officer

The amount of the annual salary and benefits for other elected and appointed officers and officials in this State with comparable responsibilities, the judiciary, and, to the extent practicable, the private sector
The responsibility and scope of authority of the entity in which the state officer serves

Whether the Director of Finance estimates that there will be a negative balance in the Special Fund for Economic Uncertainties in an amount equal to or greater than 1 percent of estimated General Fund revenues in the current fiscal year

provisions.what: Until a resolution establishing or adjusting the annual salary and benefits for state officers takes effect, each state officer shall continue to receive the same annual salary and benefits received previously

All commission members shall receive their actual and necessary expenses, including travel expenses; each member shall be compensated at the same rate as members, other than the chairperson, of the Fair Political Practices Commission, for each day engaged in official duties, not to exceed 45 days per year

The Department of Personnel Administration, the Board of Administration of the Public Employees’ Retirement System, or other appropriate agencies, or their successors, shall furnish, from existing resources, staff and services to the commission as needed
provisions.binds: The Department of Personnel Administration, the Board of Administration of the Public Employees’ Retirement System, or other appropriate agencies, or their successors

provisions.what: Definition of state officer
terms: "State officer": the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Controller, Insurance Commissioner, Secretary of State, Superintendent of Public Instruction, Treasurer, member of the State Board of Equalization, and Member of the Legislature

review.title: Proceeds from sale of surplus state property
review.plain: Proceeds from selling surplus state property shall be used to pay principal and interest on Economic Recovery Bond Act bonds; once those are paid, the proceeds shall go into the Special Fund for Economic Uncertainties or any successor fund.

provisions.what: The proceeds from the sale of surplus state property shall be used to pay the principal and interest on bonds issued pursuant to the Economic Recovery Bond Act authorized at the March 2, 2004, statewide primary election
requires: The proceeds from the sale of surplus state property occurring on or after the effective date of this section, and any proceeds from the previous sale of surplus state property that have not been expended or encumbered as of that date, shall be used to pay the principal and interest on bonds issued pursuant to the Economic Recovery Bond Act
terms: "surplus state property": does not include property purchased with revenues described in Article XIX or any other special fund moneys

provisions.what: Once the principal and interest on those bonds are fully paid, the proceeds from the sale of surplus state property shall be deposited into the Special Fund for Economic Uncertainties, or any successor fund
conditions: Once the principal and interest on those bonds are fully paid

review.title: Legislative power; initiative and referendum
review.plain: The legislative power of California is vested in the California Legislature, made up of the Senate and Assembly, but the people reserve to themselves the powers of initiative and referendum.
powers: The legislative power of this State is vested in the California Legislature
the people reserve to themselves the powers of initiative and referendum

provisions.what: The legislative power of this State is vested in the California Legislature which consists of the Senate and Assembly
The people reserve to themselves the powers of initiative and referendum

review.title: Findings on incumbency and term limits
review.plain: The people find that incumbents' unlimited terms, own retirement system, and state-paid staff create career politicians, and declare that the powers of incumbency must be limited: retirement benefits restricted, staff and support services limited, and terms limited.

provisions.what: The people find and declare that the Founding Fathers established a system of representative government based upon free, fair, and competitive elections, and that the increased concentration of political power in the hands of incumbent representatives has made our electoral system less free, less competitive, and less representative

The people find and declare that the powers of incumbency must be limited. Retirement benefits must be restricted, state-financed incumbent staff and support services limited, and limitations placed upon the number of terms which may be served

review.title: Legislature membership, terms and qualifications
review.plain: The Senate has 40 members with 4-year terms and the Assembly 80 with 2-year terms. A person may serve no more than 12 years in the Legislature. Members must be electors and meet residence and citizenship requirements. The Governor shall call an election to fill a vacancy.
limits: a person may serve no more than 12 years in the Senate, the Assembly, or both
A person is ineligible to be a member of the Legislature

provisions.what: The Senate has a membership of 40 Senators elected for 4-year terms, 20 to begin every 2 years
The Assembly has a membership of 80 members elected for 2-year terms
The terms of a Senator or a Member of the Assembly shall commence on the first Monday in December next following her or his election
During her or his lifetime a person may serve no more than 12 years in the Senate, the Assembly, or both, in any combination of terms
forbids: serving more than 12 years in the Senate, the Assembly, or both
conditions: This subdivision shall apply only to those Members of the Senate or the Assembly who are first elected to the Legislature after the effective date of this subdivision and who have not previously served in the Senate or Assembly
exceptions: Members of the Senate or Assembly who were elected before the effective date of this subdivision may serve only the number of terms allowed at the time of the last election before the effective date of this subdivision

provisions.what: Election of members of the Assembly shall be on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years. Senators shall be elected at the same time and places as members of the Assembly
exceptions: unless otherwise prescribed by the Legislature

provisions.what: A person is ineligible to be a member of the Legislature unless the person is an elector and has been a resident of the legislative district for one year, and a citizen of the United States and a resident of California for 3 years, immediately preceding the election
requires: the person is an elector
has been a resident of the legislative district for one year
a citizen of the United States and a resident of California for 3 years, immediately preceding the election
service of the full term of office to which the person is seeking to be elected would not exceed the maximum years of service permitted by subdivision (a)

provisions.what: When a vacancy occurs in the Legislature the Governor immediately shall call an election to fill the vacancy
requires: immediately call an election to fill the vacancy
conditions: When a vacancy occurs in the Legislature

review.title: Regular and special sessions
review.plain: The Legislature shall convene in regular session on the first Monday in December of each even-numbered year and adjourns at midnight on November 30 two years later. The Governor may call a special session, limited to subjects in the proclamation and incidental matters.
powers: the Governor by proclamation may cause the Legislature to assemble in special session
may provide for expenses and other matters incidental to the session
limits: has power to legislate only on subjects specified in the proclamation

provisions.what: The Legislature shall convene in regular session at noon on the first Monday in December of each even-numbered year and each house shall immediately organize
Each session of the Legislature shall adjourn sine die by operation of the Constitution at midnight on November 30 of the following even-numbered year
On extraordinary occasions the Governor by proclamation may cause the Legislature to assemble in special session
When so assembled it has power to legislate only on subjects specified in the proclamation
exceptions: but may provide for expenses and other matters incidental to the session

review.title: Legislators' outside income, travel expenses and retirement
review.plain: No Member may knowingly receive earned income from a lobbyist, lobbying firm or recent legislative contractor. Travel and living expenses are set by two-thirds statute and limited during long recesses. Legislative retirement benefits are limited.
powers: The Legislature may, prior to their retirement, limit the retirement benefits payable to Members of the Legislature
the Legislature may provide that no Member shall be deprived of a cost of living adjustment
limits: no Member of the Legislature may knowingly receive any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist or lobbying firm
may not, for a period of one year following its receipt, vote upon
A Member may not receive travel and living expenses during the times that the Legislature is in recess for more than three calendar days
The Legislature may not provide retirement benefits based on any portion of a monthly salary in excess of five hundred dollars ($500)

provisions.what: No Member of the Legislature may knowingly receive any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist or lobbying firm, as defined by the Political Reform Act of 1974, or from a person who, during the previous 12 months, has been under a contract with the Legislature
forbids: knowingly receive any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist or lobbying firm, or from a person who, during the previous 12 months, has been under a contract with the Legislature

provisions.what: The Legislature shall enact laws that define earned income
terms: "earned income": does not include any community property interest in the income of a spouse

provisions.what: Any Member who knowingly receives any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist employer may not, for a period of one year following its receipt, vote upon or make, participate in making, or in any way attempt to use his or her official position to influence an action or decision before the Legislature which he or she knows, or has reason to know, would have a direct and significant financial impact on the lobbyist employer and would not impact the public generally or a significant segment of the public in a similar manner
provisions.binds: Any Member who knowingly receives earned income from a lobbyist employer
exceptions: other than an action or decision involving a bill described in subdivision (c) of Section 12 of this article
terms: "public generally": includes an industry, trade, or profession

provisions.what: Travel and living expenses for Members of the Legislature in connection with their official duties shall be prescribed by statute passed by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership of each house concurring
A Member may not receive travel and living expenses during the times that the Legislature is in recess for more than three calendar days
exceptions: unless the Member is traveling to or from, or is in attendance at, any meeting of a committee of which he or she is a member, or a meeting, conference, or other legislative function or responsibility as authorized by the rules of the house of which he or she is a member, which is held at a location at least 20 miles from his or her place of residence

provisions.what: The Legislature may not provide retirement benefits based on any portion of a monthly salary in excess of five hundred dollars ($500) paid to any Member of the Legislature
exceptions: unless the Member receives the greater amount while serving as a Member in the Legislature

provisions.what: The Legislature may, prior to their retirement, limit the retirement benefits payable to Members of the Legislature who serve during or after the term commencing in 1967

When computing the retirement allowance of a Member who serves in the Legislature during the term commencing in 1967 or later, allowance may be made for increases in cost of living if so provided by statute, but only with respect to increases in the cost of living occurring after retirement of the Member

The Legislature may provide that no Member shall be deprived of a cost of living adjustment based on a monthly salary of five hundred dollars ($500) which has accrued prior to the commencement of the 1967 Regular Session of the Legislature

review.title: Legislators' Social Security; no other pension
review.plain: A person elected to or serving in the Legislature on or after November 1, 1990, shall participate in Social Security, with the State paying only the employer's share. No other pension or retirement benefit shall accrue from legislative service, though vested benefits are not diminished.
limits: No other pension or retirement benefit shall accrue as a result of service in the Legislature
no further entitlement to nor vesting in any existing program shall accrue to any such person

provisions.what: A person elected to or serving in the Legislature on or after November 1, 1990, shall participate in the Federal Social Security (Retirement, Disability, Health Insurance) Program and the State shall pay only the employer’s share of the contribution necessary to such participation
provisions.binds: A person elected to or serving in the Legislature on or after November 1, 1990; the State

provisions.what: No other pension or retirement benefit shall accrue as a result of service in the Legislature, such service not being intended as a career occupation
forbids: accrual of any other pension or retirement benefit as a result of service in the Legislature

provisions.what: This Section shall not be construed to abrogate or diminish any vested pension or retirement benefit which may have accrued under an existing law to a person holding or having held office in the Legislature
Upon adoption of this Act no further entitlement to nor vesting in any existing program shall accrue to any such person
exceptions: other than Social Security to the extent herein provided

review.title: Discipline and ethics of Members
review.plain: Each house judges its Members' qualifications and elections and, by two-thirds rollcall vote, may expel or suspend a Member. Members may not accept honoraria or compensation for appearing before state boards or agencies, and the Legislature shall enact laws on gifts, lobbying and conflicts of interest.
powers: Each house may suspend a Member
the house may deem the salary and benefits of the Member to be forfeited
the people reserve to themselves the power to implement this requirement
limits: shall not exercise any of the rights, privileges, duties, or powers of his or her office
No Member of the Legislature may accept any honorarium

No Member of the Legislature may knowingly accept any compensation for appearing, agreeing to appear, or taking any other action on behalf of another person before any state government board or agency
the Member may not, for a period of one year following the acceptance of the compensation, vote upon

provisions.what: Each house of the Legislature shall judge the qualifications and elections of its Members
Each house, by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, may expel a Member
conditions: by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring

provisions.what: Each house may suspend a Member by motion or resolution adopted by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, and may deem the salary and benefits of the Member to be forfeited for all or part of the period of the suspension
requires: The motion or resolution shall contain findings and declarations setting forth the basis for the suspension
conditions: by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring
by express provision of the motion or resolution

provisions.what: A Member suspended shall not exercise any of the rights, privileges, duties, or powers of his or her office, or utilize any resources of the Legislature, during the period the suspension is in effect
provisions.binds: A Member suspended pursuant to this paragraph

provisions.what: The suspension shall remain in effect until the date specified in the motion or resolution or, if no date is specified, the date a subsequent motion or resolution terminating the suspension is adopted by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership of the house concurring
No Member of the Legislature may accept any honorarium
The Legislature shall enact laws that implement this subdivision
The Legislature shall enact laws that ban or strictly limit the acceptance of a gift by a Member of the Legislature from any source if the acceptance of the gift might create a conflict of interest

No Member of the Legislature may knowingly accept any compensation for appearing, agreeing to appear, or taking any other action on behalf of another person before any state government board or agency
exceptions: a Member may engage in activities involving a board or agency which are strictly on his or her own behalf, appear in the capacity of an attorney before any court or the Workers’ Compensation Appeals Board, or act as an advocate without compensation or make an inquiry for information on behalf of a person before a board or agency
This subdivision does not prohibit any action of a partnership or firm of which the Member is a member if the Member does not share directly or indirectly in the fee

provisions.what: If a Member knowingly accepts any compensation for appearing on behalf of another person before any local government board or agency, the Member may not, for a period of one year following the acceptance of the compensation, vote upon or make, participate in making, or in any way attempt to use his or her official position to influence an action or decision before the Legislature which he or she knows, or has reason to know, would have a direct and significant financial impact on that person and would not impact the public generally or a significant segment of the public in a similar manner
provisions.binds: A Member who knowingly accepts compensation for appearing before any local government board or agency
exceptions: other than an action or decision involving a bill described in subdivision (c) of Section 12
terms: "public generally": includes an industry, trade, or profession

provisions.what: The Legislature shall enact laws that prohibit a Member of the Legislature whose term of office commences on or after December 3, 1990, from lobbying, for compensation, before the Legislature for 12 months after leaving office

The Legislature shall enact new laws, and strengthen the enforcement of existing laws, prohibiting Members of the Legislature from engaging in activities or having interests which conflict with the proper discharge of their duties and responsibilities
The people reserve to themselves the power to implement this requirement pursuant to Article II

review.title: Senate and Assembly districts
review.plain: For choosing members of the Legislature, the State is divided into 40 Senatorial and 80 Assembly districts; each Senatorial district chooses one Senator and each Assembly district one member of the Assembly.

provisions.what: For the purpose of choosing members of the Legislature, the State shall be divided into 40 Senatorial and 80 Assembly districts to be called Senatorial and Assembly Districts
Each Senatorial district shall choose one Senator and each Assembly district shall choose one member of the Assembly

review.title: Legislative proceedings, journals and open sessions
review.plain: Each house chooses its officers, adopts rules and keeps a journal. Proceedings shall be open and public, and any person may record and broadcast them; the Legislature shall post recordings online. Closed sessions are allowed only for listed purposes and party caucuses.
rights: The right to attend open and public proceedings
the right of any person to record by audio or video means any and all parts of the proceedings
shall have standing to challenge said rules
powers: may recess from day to day and compel the attendance of absent members
the Legislature may adopt reasonable rules pursuant to paragraph (5)
closed sessions may be held solely for any of the following purposes
limits: Neither house without the consent of the other may recess for more than 10 days or to any other place

provisions.what: Each house shall choose its officers and adopt rules for its proceedings
A majority of the membership constitutes a quorum
A smaller number may recess from day to day and compel the attendance of absent members
provisions.holder: A smaller number than a quorum

provisions.what: Each house shall keep and publish a journal of its proceedings
The rollcall vote of the members on a question shall be taken and entered in the journal at the request of 3 members present
conditions: at the request of 3 members present

provisions.what: The proceedings of each house and the committees thereof shall be open and public. The right to attend open and public proceedings includes the right of any person to record by audio or video means any and all parts of the proceedings and to broadcast or otherwise transmit them
provisions.binds: Each house and the committees thereof
exceptions: Except as provided in paragraph (3)

provisions.what: The Legislature may adopt reasonable rules pursuant to paragraph (5) regulating the placement and use of the equipment for recording or broadcasting the proceedings for the sole purpose of minimizing disruption of the proceedings
conditions: for the sole purpose of minimizing disruption of the proceedings

provisions.what: Any aggrieved party shall have standing to challenge said rules in an action for declaratory and injunctive relief, and the Legislature shall have the burden of demonstrating that the rule is reasonable

The Legislature shall cause audiovisual recordings to be made of all proceedings subject to paragraph (1) in their entirety, shall make such recordings public through the Internet within 24 hours after the proceedings have been recessed or adjourned for the day, and shall maintain an archive of said recordings accessible to the public through the Internet and downloadable for a period of no less than 20 years
conditions: Commencing on January 1 of the second calendar year following the adoption of this paragraph

provisions.what: Closed sessions may be held solely for any of the following purposes
requires: To consider the appointment, employment, evaluation of performance, or dismissal of a public officer or employee, to consider or hear complaints or charges brought against a Member of the Legislature or other public officer or employee, or to establish the classification or compensation of an employee of the Legislature
To consider matters affecting the safety and security of Members of the Legislature or its employees or the safety and security of any buildings and grounds used by the Legislature

To confer with, or receive advice from, its legal counsel regarding pending or reasonably anticipated, or whether to initiate, litigation when discussion in open session would not protect the interests of the house or committee regarding the litigation

provisions.what: A caucus of the Members of the Senate, the Members of the Assembly, or the Members of both houses, which is composed of the members of the same political party, may meet in closed session
provisions.holder: A caucus composed of the members of the same political party

provisions.what: The Legislature shall implement this subdivision by concurrent resolution adopted by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership of each house concurring, or by statute, and in the case of a closed session held pursuant to paragraph (3), shall prescribe that reasonable notice of the closed session and the purpose of the closed session shall be provided to the public
If there is a conflict between a concurrent resolution and statute, the last adopted or enacted shall prevail
Neither house without the consent of the other may recess for more than 10 days or to any other place
conditions: without the consent of the other

review.title: Limit on Legislature's spending
review.plain: The Legislature's total spending on member and employee compensation and operating expenses may not exceed, in the first fiscal year after adoption, $950,000 per member or 80 percent of the prior year's amount, whichever is less; afterward, the prior year's amount adjusted by the State appropriations limit.
limits: may not exceed an amount equal to nine hundred fifty thousand dollars ($950,000) per member
the total aggregate expenditures may not exceed an amount equal to that expended for those purposes in the preceding fiscal year

provisions.what: In the fiscal year immediately following the adoption of this Act, the total aggregate expenditures of the Legislature for the compensation of members and employees of, and the operating expenses and equipment for, the Legislature may not exceed an amount equal to nine hundred fifty thousand dollars ($950,000) per member for that fiscal year or 80 percent of the amount of money expended for those purposes in the preceding fiscal year, whichever is less

For each fiscal year thereafter, the total aggregate expenditures may not exceed an amount equal to that expended for those purposes in the preceding fiscal year, adjusted and compounded by an amount equal to the percentage increase in the appropriations limit for the State established pursuant to Article XIII B

review.title: Passing bills; when statutes take effect
review.plain: At regular sessions no bill but the budget bill may be acted on until the 31st day after introduction. Bills must be read on 3 days, published online 72 hours before the vote, and passed by a majority of each house. It sets when statutes take effect.
powers: the house may dispense with this requirement
limits: no bill other than the budget bill may be heard or acted on by committee or either house until the 31st day after the bill is introduced
The Legislature may make no law except by statute and may enact no statute except by bill
No bill may be passed unless it is read by title on 3 days in each house
No bill may be passed or ultimately become a statute unless the bill with any amendments has been printed, distributed to the members, and published on the Internet
